If you have seen the movie National Treasure, you might think that a treasure map was written on the back of the Declaration of Independence. However, this is not true. Although there is writing on the back of the document, it is not a treasure map. The words written on the back of the Declaration of Independence are "Original Declaration of Independence dated 4 July 1776." The text appears toward the bottom of the document, upside down. Although nobody knows for certain who wrote it, it is known that early in its history, the large parchment document, measuring 29¾ by 24½ inches, was rolled up for storage. Therefore, the inscription was probably added simply as a label.

The 800-mile Trans-Alaska Pipeline System was shut down after thousands of barrels of crude oil spilled south of Fairbanks, Alaska. The 800-mile Trans-Alaska Pipeline System was shut down after thousands of barrels of crude oil spilled south of Fairbanks, Alaska. A valve opening allows the system to release pressure, directing oil through a pipe into a tank capable of holding 55,000 barrels (2.3 million gallons). As of Wednesday afternoon, oil was still leaking from the tank's vents, apparently because of excessive vapor buildup inside the tank. A secondary containment area beneath the tanks, with a capacity of 104,500 barrels, had not yet reached its full capacity.

For much of the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, it was believed that New Zealand's first inhabitants were the Māori, who hunted large birds called moas. A later theory proposed that the Māori migrated from Polynesia in a great fleet and took New Zealand from the Moriori to establish an agricultural society. However, new evidence suggests that the Moriori were a group of mainland Māori who migrated from New Zealand to the Chatham Islands, where they developed their own distinctive, peaceful culture. Another Māori tribe also settled on the Chatham Islands after migrating from New Zealand. They called themselves Moriori, and several conflicts occurred between the groups, eventually leading to the destruction of the Moriori population.

There are several ways to purify water, and some are more effective against particular hazards than others. In some areas, boiling water for one minute is sufficient, while in others, several minutes are necessary. Filters vary in effectiveness, and if you are concerned about water safety, you should consider buying water in a sealed bottle from a reputable company.

Parisians have a reputation for being selfish, rude, and arrogant. Although this is often an unfair stereotype, the best way to get along in Paris is to be polite and behave like a well-mannered person. This will make your trip considerably easier. If you show basic courtesy, the apparent rudeness of Parisians will quickly disappear.

The rule of thirds is often used as a guideline for creating movement in a photograph while maintaining balance and composition. It states that the most effective position for the main subject is at the intersection of lines that divide an image into three equal parts vertically and horizontally.

During World War II, Germany was a common enemy, which paved the way for cooperation between Russia and the United States. By the end of the war, conflicts between their political systems, practices, and cultures had caused their relationship to deteriorate. Two years after the war ended, the former allies became enemies, and the Cold War began. This conflict continued for approximately 40 years, with proxy forces fighting in locations across Africa and Asia, including Afghanistan, Cuba, and numerous other places.

More than four million people traveled to Rome to attend the funeral. The number of attendees was so large that not everyone could reach St. Peter's Square for the funeral ceremony. Several large television screens were installed throughout Rome so people could watch the event. Similar arrangements were made in many other cities in Italy and around the world, particularly in Poland, where large crowds gathered to watch.

At approximately 9:30 a.m. local time (02:30 UTC), a JAS 39C Gripen crashed onto the runway and exploded, forcing the airport to suspend commercial flights. The pilot was identified as Squadron Leader Dilokrit Pattavee. Local media reported that an airport fire truck overturned while responding to the incident.

The Il-76 has been a major component of the Russian and Soviet armed forces since the 1970s, and it had been involved in a serious accident in Russia the previous month. On October 7, an engine separated from an aircraft immediately after takeoff, but there were no casualties. Following that incident, Russia withdrew its Il-76 aircraft from service.

Not everyone supported the inclusion of women in boxing. Amir Khan, a silver medalist at the 2004 Olympics, said, "Personally, I don't think women should fight. That's my opinion." Despite his previous comments, he said he would support British female competitors at the 2012 Olympic Games in London.

The unmanned lunar orbiter Chandrayaan-1 released its Moon Impact Probe, which traveled toward the lunar surface at a speed of 1.5 kilometers per second (3,000 miles per hour) and successfully landed near the Moon's south pole. In addition to carrying three important scientific instruments, the lunar probe had India's national flag painted on all its sides.

Today, providing luxurious bed-and-breakfast accommodation has become something of an art form in developed countries. Bed-and-breakfast establishments compete primarily on two important features: bedding and breakfast. Consequently, guests at the finest establishments can expect exceptionally luxurious beds, perhaps with handmade quilts or antique bedding. Breakfast may include seasonal regional specialties or the host's signature dish. The setting might be a historic old building decorated with antique furnishings, beautifully maintained lawns, and a swimming pool.

Most of the work carried out was largely theoretical, but the program was designed to establish a reliable model for observations of the Bridge Galaxy. The effects the team was looking for were expected to result from tidal interactions between the dark matter of the Bridge Galaxy and that of the Milky Way. Just as the Moon exerts a gravitational pull on Earth, producing tides, the Milky Way exerts a force on the Bridge Galaxy. Scientists concluded that dark matter affects other dark matter in much the same way that ordinary matter does. According to this theory, most of the galaxy's dark matter exists in a halo surrounding it and consists of many small particles.

Personal VPN (Virtual Private Network) providers are an excellent way to bypass both political censorship and commercial IP-based geographic restrictions. They are better than web proxies for several reasons: they reroute all Internet traffic, not just HTTP traffic. They generally offer higher bandwidth and better service quality. They also encrypt connections, making surveillance considerably more difficult.

Time is something that surrounds us and affects everything we do, yet it is difficult to understand. Religious scholars, philosophers, and scientists have studied time for thousands of years. We experience time as a sequence of events moving from the future through the present into the past. Time also allows us to compare the durations of events. You can measure the passage of time yourself by observing the repetition of a cyclical event. A cyclical event is something that occurs repeatedly at regular intervals.

You should carefully choose your frequent-flyer airline within an airline alliance. Although it may seem obvious to select the airline you travel with most often, you should also be aware that the benefits offered vary and that frequent-flyer points may be more generous with another airline in the same alliance.

NHK also reported that the Kashiwazaki-Kariwa Nuclear Power Plant in Niigata Prefecture was operating normally. Hokuriku Electric Power Company reported no earthquake-related damage and stated that reactors 1 and 2 at the Shika Nuclear Power Plant had been shut down. Approximately 9,400 households in the area reportedly had no water, while about 100 households were without electricity. Some roads in affected areas were damaged, railway services were disrupted, and Noto Airport in Ishikawa was also closed.

Middle-distance running is a relatively inexpensive sport. However, there are many misconceptions about the equipment needed to participate. Products can be purchased as necessary, but most will have little or no real effect on performance. Athletes may feel that they prefer certain products even when those products provide no actual benefit.

Australian Treasurer Peter Costello, who was widely expected to succeed Prime Minister John Howard as leader of the Liberal Party, announced his support for developing a nuclear power industry in Australia. Mr. Costello said Australia should begin using nuclear power when its production becomes economically viable. "If it becomes commercially viable, we should have it," Mr. Costello said. "In principle, there is no objection to nuclear energy."

If you visit the Arctic or Antarctic regions during winter, you will experience the polar night, which means the Sun does not rise above the horizon. This provides an excellent opportunity to see the aurora borealis, as the sky will remain dark almost all the time. Because these regions are sparsely populated, light pollution is usually not a problem, so you can also enjoy observing the stars.

A civilization is a distinct culture shared by a particular group of people who live and work together cooperatively as a society. The word "civilization" comes from the Latin word "civilis," meaning relating to a citizen, which is connected to the Latin words "civis," meaning citizen, and "civitas," meaning city or city-state. These terms also indicate something about the size of a society. City-states were the precursors of nations. A civilized culture involves passing knowledge and arts down through many generations, establishing a lasting cultural legacy, and ensuring its proper transmission. Smaller cultures often disappear without leaving sufficient historical evidence and therefore fail to be recognized as complete civilizations.

The incident occurred among high mountains and is believed to have resulted from enemy gunfire. Efforts to locate the crash site are being hampered by bad weather and extremely rugged terrain.

The Indus Valley Civilization was a Bronze Age civilization in northwestern South Asia, covering most of present-day Pakistan, parts of northwestern India, and northeastern Afghanistan. The civilization flourished in the valleys of the Indus River, from which it takes its name. However, some scholars suggest that, because the civilization also existed in the basin of the now-dried-up Saraswati River, it should more appropriately be called the Indus-Saraswati Civilization. Others call it the Harappan Civilization, after Harappa, the first of its sites to be excavated in the 1920s.

One disadvantage of zoom lenses is their optical complexity and the large number of lens elements required to achieve a range of focal lengths, far more than in prime lenses. This issue is becoming less significant as lens manufacturers achieve higher production standards. As a result, zoom lenses can now produce images of quality comparable to those obtained with fixed-focal-length lenses. Another disadvantage is that the maximum aperture, or speed, of a zoom lens is generally smaller. An inexpensive zoom lens can be very difficult to use in low light without a flash.

The Temple of Artemis at Ephesus was destroyed by arson committed by Herostratus on July 21, 356 BC. According to the story, his goal was to achieve fame at any cost. Overcome with grief, the inhabitants declared that his name should never be recorded. However, the Greek historian Strabo later recorded his name, which is why we know it today. The temple was destroyed on the very night Alexander the Great was born. As king, Alexander offered to pay for the temple's reconstruction, but his offer was rejected. Later, after Alexander's death, the temple was rebuilt in 323 BC.

The sites and wildlife of the Galápagos Islands are best experienced by boat, as Charles Darwin did in 1835. More than 60 cruise vessels operate in Galápagos waters, accommodating between 8 and 100 passengers. Most people book their places in advance because boats generally fill up during the peak season. Make sure the agent you book with is a Galápagos specialist who has extensive knowledge of different types of vessels. This will ensure that your particular interests and any limitations are matched with the vessel best suited to your needs.

Bowen Island is popular for day trips and relaxing weekend getaways, offering kayaking, hiking, shopping, restaurants, and much more. This charming community is located in Howe Sound, a short distance from Vancouver, and is easily accessible by water taxis departing from Granville Island in downtown Vancouver. For those who enjoy outdoor activities, a trip along the Sea-to-Sky Corridor is a must. Whistler, about a 1.5-hour drive from Vancouver, is expensive but famous for hosting the 2010 Winter Olympics. In winter, enjoy some of the best skiing in North America, and in summer, try some excellent mountain biking.

Drink alcoholic beverages in moderation. Alcohol affects everyone differently, so knowing your limits is very important. Possible long-term health consequences of excessive drinking include liver damage, blindness, and even death. The potential risks increase when illegally produced alcohol is consumed. Illicit spirits may contain dangerous impurities, including methanol, which can cause blindness or death even in small amounts.

The Sun does not have a solid surface like Earth that you can stand on. The Sun is made entirely of gases, fire, and plasma. As you move away from the Sun's center, the gas becomes progressively thinner. The outer part of the Sun that we can see is called the photosphere, which means "sphere of light."

Technological determinism is a term encompassing a wide range of theories, from the idea that technological progress or modern technology is inevitable to the strong belief that human destiny is governed by scientific laws and an underlying logic associated with their expression in technology. Most interpretations of technological determinism share two general ideas: that technological development follows its own path independently of cultural or political influences, and that technology, in turn, produces effects on societies that are inherent rather than socially conditioned. For example, one might argue that the automobile inevitably leads to the development of roads. However, building a nationwide road network for only a few cars would not be economically worthwhile, so new production methods were developed to reduce the cost of car ownership. Widespread car ownership also leads to higher rates of road accidents, encouraging the development of new medical techniques to repair damaged bodies.

The Babylonians maintained a principal place of worship for each of their gods, which was considered the god's home. People brought offerings to the gods, and priests tried to provide for the gods' needs during ceremonies and festivals. Each temple contained an open courtyard and an inner sanctuary that only priests could enter. Sometimes special pyramid-shaped towers, known as ziggurats, were constructed as part of the temples. The uppermost part of the tower was a special sacred place reserved for the god.

Because Montevideo lies south of the equator, it experiences summer when the Northern Hemisphere has winter, and vice versa. Montevideo is in the subtropics, and temperatures above 30°C are common during the summer months. Winter can be surprisingly cold: temperatures occasionally fall below freezing, while wind and humidity can make the weather feel much colder than the thermometer indicates. There is no distinct rainy or dry season, as rainfall is distributed fairly evenly throughout the year.

After the Battle of France ended, Germany began preparing to invade the island of Great Britain. Germany named the planned invasion "Operation Sea Lion." When the British Army was evacuated from Dunkirk, it had abandoned most of its heavy weapons and equipment, leaving it considerably weakened. However, the Royal Navy was still capable of defeating the German Navy, or Kriegsmarine, and destroying any invasion fleet sent across the English Channel. Nevertheless, only a few Royal Navy ships were stationed near the likely invasion routes because the admirals feared that German aircraft would attack and sink them.

Overscan is one of the most common problems encountered when converting a film into DVD format. Most televisions are designed to provide a pleasing viewing experience. As a result, the edges of everything you see on television are cropped at the top, bottom, and sides. This is done to ensure that the picture fills the entire screen, and it is called overscan. Unfortunately, when you create a DVD, its edges may be cut off, and subtitles at the bottom of the video may not be fully visible.

The Hershey-Chase experiment was crucial in establishing DNA as the genetic material. Hershey and Chase used bacteriophages, or viruses, to inject their DNA into bacteria. They conducted two experiments, using radioactive phosphorus to label the DNA of the phages in one experiment and radioactive sulfur to label their proteins in the other.

California Governor Arnold Schwarzenegger signed a bill that would prohibit the sale of violent video games to young children. Under the bill, violent video games sold in California would have to carry an "18" age-rating label, and violations of the sales restriction would be punishable by a fine of $1,000 per offense.

Army ants also build nests and establish new colonies in different phases. During the nomadic phase, the army of ants marches at night and stops to rest during the day. A colony enters the nomadic phase when available food supplies become scarce. During this phase, the colony builds temporary nests that change every day. Each of these nomadic periods, involving swarming and marching, lasts approximately 17 days.

The official currency of the Falkland Islands is the Falkland Islands pound (FKP), which is pegged at equal value to the British pound (GBP). Money can be exchanged at the islands' only bank, located opposite the FIC West Store in Stanley. British pounds are generally accepted throughout the islands, while credit cards are accepted in Stanley and US dollars are also frequently accepted. Credit cards are unlikely to be accepted on the outer islands, although British, European, and American currency may be accepted. Check with the owners in advance to determine which payment methods they accept. It is almost impossible to exchange Falkland Islands currency outside the islands, so exchange your money before leaving.

Anyone visiting a country that could be considered a war zone should obtain professional training. An internet search for a "hostile environment course" will probably help you find a local company offering such training. The course will cover all the issues discussed here in detail, usually with practical exercises. A typical course lasts two to five days and includes role-playing, extensive first-aid training, and sometimes weapons training. Books and magazines about wilderness survival are common, but publications specifically about war zones are less widely available.

İzmir is Turkey's third-largest city, with a population of approximately 3.7 million, its second-largest port after Istanbul, and an excellent transportation hub. The once-ancient city of Smyrna is now a modern, developed, and busy commercial center situated around a large bay and surrounded by mountains. Its wide boulevards, glass-fronted buildings, and modern shopping centers, alongside red-tiled roofs, an 18th-century bazaar, old mosques, and churches, give the city a more Mediterranean European atmosphere than a traditional Turkish one.

The D-Day landings and the battles that followed resulted in the liberation of northern France, but the south had not yet been liberated. It was governed by the "Vichy" French, a puppet government of France. These were French people who had made peace with Germany in 1940 and cooperated with the invaders rather than fighting them. On August 15, 1940, Allied forces invaded southern France in an attack called "Operation Dragoon." In just two weeks, American and Free French forces liberated southern France and were advancing toward Germany.

A hospitality exchange network is an organization that connects travelers with local residents in the cities they plan to visit. Joining such a network usually requires filling out an online form, although some networks offer or require additional verification. A list of available hosts is then provided in print or online, sometimes including references and reviews from other travelers. Computer programmer Casey Fenton founded Couchsurfing in January 2004 after finding a cheap flight to Iceland but being unable to find suitable accommodation. He emailed students at a local university and received an overwhelming number of offers of free accommodation.

In France, voting has traditionally been a low-tech process. Voters enter a voting booth, mark their preferred candidate on a preprinted paper ballot, and place it in an envelope. After officials verify the voter's identity, the voter puts the envelope into the ballot box and signs the electoral register. French electoral law strictly regulates these procedures. Since 1988, ballot boxes have been required to be transparent so that voters and observers can see that no envelopes are present at the beginning of voting and that no envelopes are added except those of authorized voters, which are carefully counted. Candidates have the right to send representatives to monitor every stage of the process. In the evening, volunteers count the votes under strict supervision and according to specific procedures.

The Olympic gold medalist was a swimmer who competed in three Commonwealth Games relays and the 100-meter and 200-meter freestyle events, but concerns about his health arose because of his medical complaints. He cannot take the medications he needs for pain relief because those drugs are prohibited during the Games.

Approximately 200 running tour organizations operate internationally, most of them independently. Go Running Tours, the successor to Global Running Tours, has a network of dozens of sightseeing running tour providers across four continents. Starting with Running Tours Barcelona in Barcelona and Running Tours Copenhagen in Copenhagen, the network quickly expanded to include Prague Tours in Prague and other locations.

Backpacking on skis across snow is also known as backcountry skiing, ski touring, or ski hiking. It is related to, but generally does not include, Alpine-style ski touring or mountaineering, the latter being practiced on steep terrain and requiring stiffer skis and boots. Think of a skiing route in much the same way as a hiking or walking route. In good conditions, you can cover considerably more distance than you would on foot, but you will rarely achieve the speed of cross-country skiing on prepared tracks while carrying a heavy backpack.

The tourist season at hill stations generally peaks during the Indian summer. However, winter brings a different kind of beauty and charm. Many hill stations receive substantial snowfall, making skiing and snowboarding especially popular activities.

South Africa defeated the All Blacks of New Zealand in a Tri Nations rugby union match played at the Royal Bafokeng Stadium in Rustenburg, South Africa. The final score was 21–20, a one-point victory that ended the All Blacks' 15-match winning streak. The Springboks finally broke their own streak of five consecutive defeats. This was the final match for the All Blacks, who had already won the trophy two weeks earlier. The final match of the series will take place next week at Ellis Park in Johannesburg, where the Springboks will face Australia.

Approximately 400,000 cases of multiple sclerosis have been reported across the United States, making it the leading neurological disease among young and middle-aged adults. Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a disease that affects the central nervous system, which consists of the brain, spinal cord, and optic nerves. Research has shown that women are twice as likely as men to develop MS.

The photographer was taken to Ronald Reagan UCLA Medical Center, where he died. He was reportedly around 20 years old. Tutankhamun's Tomb (KV62) — Discovered by Howard Carter in 1922, the burial site of the young king is perhaps one of the most famous tombs in the Valley of the Kings. Compared with most other royal tombs, however, Tutankhamun's tomb is very small, has limited decoration, and is barely worth visiting. Anyone hoping to examine the damage caused during attempts to remove the mummy from its coffin will be disappointed, as only the head and shoulders are visible. The valuable artifacts that made the tomb famous are no longer there, having been transferred to the Egyptian Museum in Cairo. Visitors with limited time would be better off spending it elsewhere.

Canyoning involves descending into a river gorge, which may be either dry or filled with water. Canyoning combines elements of swimming, climbing, and jumping, but it requires relatively little training and physical fitness to get started, especially compared with activities such as rock climbing, scuba diving, or Alpine skiing.

Over the past three decades, China has developed a market economy despite officially remaining a communist state. The first economic reforms were introduced under the leadership of Deng Xiaoping. Since then, China's economy has grown ninetyfold. For the first time, China exported more cars than Germany last year and also surpassed the United States in automobile production. China's GDP could grow substantially larger than that of the United States over the next two decades.

If this discovery is confirmed, it will bring an end to the eight-year search for the Musashi. After the seabed was mapped, the sunken wreck was located using a remotely operated vehicle (ROV). Paul Allen, one of the world's wealthiest people, reportedly spent much of his fortune on marine exploration and continued searching for the Musashi because of his lifelong interest in warfare.

After Congress adopted it on July 4, a handwritten draft signed by Congress President John Hancock and Secretary Charles Thomson was sent a few blocks away to John Dunlap's printing shop. Between 150 and 200 copies were produced overnight, now known as the "Dunlap Broadsides." The document was first read publicly by John Nixon in the courtyard of Independence Hall on July 8. A copy was sent to George Washington on July 6, and he had it read aloud to his troops in New York on July 9. One copy reached London on August 10. The 25 Dunlap Broadsides known to survive are the oldest existing copies of the document. The original manuscript has been lost.

Immediately after hostilities began, Britain imposed a naval blockade on Germany. This strategy proved effective, cutting off vital military and civilian supplies, although the blockade violated generally accepted principles of international law established through international treaties over previous centuries. Britain laid mines throughout international waters to prevent ships from entering large areas of the sea, thereby endangering neutral vessels as well. Because the response to this tactic was very limited, Germany expected that unrestricted submarine warfare would provoke a similarly limited reaction.

A backcountry permit is required to camp below the rim of the Grand Canyon. Permits are limited to protect the canyon and become available on the first day of the month, four months before the month in which the trip begins. For example, backcountry permits for any starting date in May become available on January 1. The most popular locations, such as Bright Angel Campground near Phantom Ranch, are usually fully booked through applications received on the first day reservations open. A limited number of permits are reserved for walk-in applications and are issued on a first-come, first-served basis.

Scientists have discovered geological formations called lobate scarps on the Moon's surface, which have formed very slowly as the Moon contracts. These features, found across the lunar surface, show little evidence of weathering. This suggests that the geological events responsible for their formation occurred relatively recently. The findings challenge the claim that the Moon is completely geologically inactive.

The South Pole Traverse, also known as the South Pole Highway, is a 1,600-kilometer route from McMurdo Station on the Ross Sea to the South Pole. Its path is marked by flags attached to poles driven into the snow. Only specialized tractors pulling sledges loaded with fuel and supplies can travel along this route. These vehicles are very slow, so the traverse must make a long detour around the Transantarctic Mountains to reach the plateau.

There are several theories about how Sanskrit originated. One suggests that the Aryans migrated to India from the west, bringing their language with them. Sanskrit is an ancient language comparable to Latin, which was spoken in Europe. The world's oldest known book was written in Sanskrit. After the Upanishads were compiled, Sanskrit declined because of the influence of religious leaders. Sanskrit is an extremely complex and rich language that served as the source of several modern Indian languages, just as Latin provided the foundation for European languages such as French and Spanish.

If you want to fly entirely around the world in the Southern Hemisphere, your choice of flights and destinations is limited because of the lack of transoceanic routes. No airline alliance covers all three ocean crossings in the Southern Hemisphere, and SkyTeam does not cover any of them. However, Star Alliance covers all regions except the southeastern Pacific route from Santiago, Chile, to Tahiti, which is a LATAM Oneworld flight. If you do not wish to visit the South Pacific or the west coast of South America, this flight is not your only option. (See below.)

Since the ability to acquire knowledge and learn has changed in the ways described above, the basic approach to acquiring knowledge has also changed. This view of obtaining information was different: individual memorization was no longer emphasized, while the ability to remember texts became a greater focus. In short, the Renaissance brought about a significant change in approaches to learning and the dissemination of knowledge.

Depending on the importance of the genetic material affected and whether the affected cells are germ cells, mutations can have different kinds of effects. Only mutations occurring in germline cells can be passed on to children, while mutations elsewhere can cause cell death or cancer.

Lions are the most social members of the cat family, living in large groups called prides. A pride consists of approximately thirty females and cubs, along with one to three related adult males. The females are usually closely related, forming a large family of sisters and daughters. Lion prides function much like packs of wolves or dogs. Surprisingly, these animals exhibit behaviors similar to those of lions, unlike other big cats, and are extremely dangerous to their prey.

Registration is an additional requirement in the visa process. In some countries, you must register your presence and the address where you are staying with the local authorities. This may require filling out a form at the local police station or visiting an immigration office. In many countries with such laws, local hotels will handle the registration for you, although it is worth asking. In other cases, only people staying outside tourist accommodations need to register.

Sightseeing trips are economical for larger groups, so if you are traveling alone or with one friend, try meeting other people and forming a group of four to six to obtain a lower rate per person. However, this should not really concern you, because tourists are often moved from one vehicle to another simply to fill the vehicles. In fact, this seems to be a trick used to convince people that they should pay more.

Many people have observed that rhythms in activity and behavior often depend on the presence of internal cycles and biological clocks. Such regular rhythms, which are not merely responses to recurring external signals, have been documented in most living organisms, including bacteria, fungi, plants, and animals. A biological clock is a self-sustaining oscillator that continues to maintain its cycle independently, even in the absence of external signals.

After the dam was constructed in 1963, the seasonal floods that distributed sediment throughout the river were stopped. This sediment was essential for forming sandbars and beaches that serve as wildlife habitats. As a result, two fish species have become extinct, while two others, including the humpback chub, have become endangered. Although the water level will rise only a few feet during the flood, officials expect this to be enough to restore the sandbars that have been washed away by the current.

Madhya Pradesh police have recovered the stolen laptop and mobile phone. Deputy Inspector General D. K. Arya said, "We have arrested five men who raped the Swiss woman and recovered the victim's mobile phone and laptop from them." The suspects have been identified as Baba Kanjar, Bhuta Kanjar, Rampro Kanjar, Gajah Kanjar, and Vishno Kanjar. Superintendent of Police Chandrashekhar Solanki said the suspects were presented in court with their faces covered.

The postmodern approach to education offers freedom from absolutes. There is no single best way to learn. In fact, there is no single best thing to learn. Learning occurs through the experience between the learner and the knowledge being presented. Educational television shows that demonstrate how to perform tasks and provide information illustrate this point. Many of us find ourselves watching television programs about activities or experiences in which we will never participate or apply the knowledge we gain. We may never repair a car, build a waterfall in our backyard, hike to examine ancient ruins, or renovate our neighbor's house.

Taiwan's history began in the fifteenth century, when European sailors passing by recorded the island's name as Ilha Formosa, meaning "Beautiful Island." In 1624, the Dutch East India Company established a base in southwestern Taiwan, began changing indigenous agricultural practices, and employed Chinese workers on its rice and sugar plantations. In 1683, forces of the Qing Dynasty (1644–1912) took control of Taiwan's western and eastern coastal regions, and in 1885 Taiwan was declared a province of the Qing Empire. In 1895, following defeat in the First Sino-Japanese War (1894–1895), the Qing government signed the Treaty of Shimonoseki, under which it ceded sovereignty over Taiwan to Japan, which ruled the island until 1945.

Giancarlo Fisichella lost control of his car and ended his race shortly after the start. His teammate Fernando Alonso had been leading for most of the race, but his race ended in the pit stop, apparently because a front wheel became badly stuck. Michael Schumacher ended his race shortly after Alonso, having suffered damage during several collisions throughout the race.

Children develop awareness of racial and ethnic stereotypes at a very young age, and these stereotypes influence their behavior. For example, children belonging to racial minorities who are stereotyped as performing poorly in school may become less motivated to do well academically once they become aware of the stereotypes associated with their race.

Because many pueblos are quite remote, you cannot experience much nightlife without traveling toward Albuquerque or Santa Fe. However, almost all the casinos listed above serve alcoholic beverages, and many feature well-known entertainment acts, particularly the larger casinos immediately surrounding Albuquerque and Santa Fe. Be warned that bars or drinking establishments in small settlements are not always welcoming places for outsiders to visit and spend time. Another concern is that northern New Mexico has significant problems with drunk driving, and the concentration of intoxicated drivers is considerably higher near bars in smaller communities.

Asynchronous communication increases the time available for feedback and responses to others. This allows students to work at their own pace and control the speed at which they receive instructional information. Furthermore, with the possibility of flexible working hours, there will be relatively few time constraints (Bremer, 1998). The use of the Internet and the World Wide Web has enabled learners to access information at any time. Students can submit questions to their instructors at any hour of the day and expect relatively quick responses instead of waiting for their next face-to-face meeting.

Martelly swore in a new nine-member Provisional Electoral Council (CEP) the previous day. This was Martelly's fifth CEP in four years. The previous month, a presidential commission had recommended the early resignation of the CEP as part of a package of measures intended to guide the country toward new elections. The commission was Martelly's response to anti-government protests that began in October. The failure to hold elections had sparked occasional violent demonstrations, with some elections having been postponed since 2011.

A World's Fair, commonly known as a world exposition or simply an expo, is a large international festival of arts and sciences. Participating countries present artistic and educational displays in national pavilions to highlight global issues or showcase their country's culture and history. International horticultural exhibitions are special events featuring flower displays, botanical gardens, and various exhibits related to plants.
